documents.title: Board Meeting Outcome for Standalone And Consolidated Financial Results For The Quarter Ended June 30,2026
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018
Board Meeting Intimation for Approval Of Standalone And Consolidated Un-Audited Financial Results For The Quarter Ended June 30 2026.

analysis.summary: Chembond Chemicals Limited reported consolidated FY26 revenue of Rs. 326.15 crores, representing a 12% year-on-year growth driven mainly by its water technologies segment. Consolidated H2 revenue grew 35% over H1 to Rs. 188 crores, supported by robust volume growth and strong order inflows across business units. Management highlighted raw material cost pressures and metal price volatility beginning late February and March, impacting immediate monthly margins by roughly 3%.

guidance.claim: Revenue outlook remains positive across segments, although profitability faces near-term earnings challenges.
guidance.quote: Revenue outlook continues to remain positive. However, on the earnings, profitability is a little bit of a challenge right now.

guidance.claim: The company foresees around 15% to 20% volume growth in construction chemicals in Q1.
guidance.quote: Coming to quarter one of this year, we foresee around 15 to 20% of volume growth in construction chemicals.

guidance.claim: Management expects volume growth in water chemicals to be roughly 10%.
guidance.quote: Water chemicals, it would be roughly around 10%.

demand_outlook.claim: H2 revenue across business units witnessed growth, with water technologies up 36%, construction up 18%, distribution up 40%, and cleaning and hygiene up 15%.
demand_outlook.quote: Water technologies grew 36%, construction 18%, distribution 40%, and cleaning and hygiene 15%.

demand_outlook.claim: All business units possess strong sales pipelines supporting a positive sales growth outlook.
demand_outlook.quote: All of these businesses are having strong sales pipelines and we see that the sales growth outlook looks positive across all these business units.

demand_outlook.claim: Construction chemicals revenue increased 20% in H2 to Rs. 13 crores compared to Rs. 11 crores in H1.
demand_outlook.quote: Coming to numbers on construction chemicals, so first half year was Rs. 11 crores and second half we were at Rs. 13 crores. So this is a 20% increase over first half year.

capex_expansion.claim: The company intends to deploy funds into network growth and geographical expansion.
capex_expansion.quote: We intend to deploy some of it in network growth and geographical expansion.

capex_expansion.claim: The company invested ₹90.76 lakhs towards the installation of the 350 kVA solar power plant in Gujarat during FY 2025-26.
capex_expansion.quote: ₹90.76 lakhs were invested towards installation of the 350 kVA solar renewable energy plant at the Dudhwada, Gujarat manufacturing site during FY 2025-26.

margins_costs.claim: Full-year consolidated EBITDA reached Rs. 51 crores and consolidated PBT reached Rs. 45 crores, both up 7% over the prior year.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA for the full financial year is at Rs.51 crores, up 7% over prior. Consolidated PBT is at Rs. 45 crores, 7% improvement over prior.

margins_costs.claim: Raw material costs started rising from late February and March following earlier volatility in metals.
margins_costs.quote: Material costs started increasing from March, end of Feb, March. A lot of volatility in metals before that.

orders_capacity.claim: The company is starting the financial year with a strong order book for its chemicals business.
orders_capacity.quote: So we are starting this financial year with a strong order book for our chemicals business also.

orders_capacity.claim: Water BU entered the financial year with a strong order book for both chemicals and equipment.
orders_capacity.quote: Water BU, we are entering this, as I mentioned earlier, with a strong order book for chemicals as well as for the equipment.

capital_allocation.claim: Construction chemicals maintains days sales outstanding at around 88 days as on March 31, 2026.
capital_allocation.quote: We are maintaining a tight credit policy and our day sales outstanding for construction chemicals is around 88 days as on 31st of March 2026.

capital_allocation.claim: The company has around Rs. 65 crores on its books.
capital_allocation.quote: Yes, we have around sixty-five crores on books.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of ₹1.25 per equity share of face value ₹5 each, aggregating to ₹336.20 lakhs for FY 2025-26.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of ₹1.25 (Rupee One and Paise Twenty-Five only) per equity share of ₹5 (Rupees Five only) each, aggregating to ₹336.20 lakhs for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

risks_headwinds.claim: Public sector units represent about 30% of the water business and refused force majeure until government declaration.
risks_headwinds.quote: About 30 percent of our total business in the water business comes from public sector units, and none of them had accepted a force majeure until the government just declared it two weeks ago.

risks_headwinds.claim: Public sector customers refuse to amend contractual terms for price adjustments.
risks_headwinds.quote: Public sector is a different story. They are refusing to amend the terms.

management_commitments.claim: Management foresees volume growth of 15% to 20% in construction chemicals in Q1.
management_commitments.quote: Coming to quarter one of this year, we foresee around 15 to 20% of volume growth in construction chemicals.

management_commitments.claim: Management expects volume growth in water chemicals to be roughly 10%.
management_commitments.quote: Water chemicals, it would be roughly around 10%.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
